text.p: Infrastructure Trust said on Tuesday it had requested that its securities be suspended from trading pending an announcement on the successful bidder for the Loy Yang A power station in Victoria.
The request follows a trading halt placed on the stock on Monday.
Infrastructure units closed on Friday three cents lower at A$1.27.
The sale of the 2,000 megawatt station and associated coal mine was likely to fetch around A$4.5 billion for the Victorian state government, a source told Reuters last week.
This compares with a value of between A$4.75 billion to A$5.00 billion quoted in recent newspaper reports.
Final bids for Loy Yang A, the biggest and most modern power station to be privatised by the Victoria government, closed last Thursday.
The announcement of the winning bid was expected to be announced today by the Victorian government in Melbourne at around 12.30 p.m (0230 GMT). -- Sydney Newsroom 612 9373-1800
